title: VESPER Trigger
description: IC-008. The data structure that makes autonomy an engineered control system rather than a prompt. COC ARCH-28 forbids cron; ARCH-04 forbids asking an LLM to invent tasks. A Trigger is the third option: a DETERMINISTIC predicate over world-model state decides WHETHER a goal exists; a model decides only HOW to satisfy one already justified. Authority: DR-005, RB-005, RB-006, RB-018, RB-019, ARCH-04, ARCH-12, ARCH-28; REM-007, REM-008.

predicate.description: A total, side-effect-free, provably terminating expression over four typed domains: world facts, task graph, schedule, event patterns. Evaluated by DF-TRIGGER-EVAL inside a sandbox holding NO model capability (INV-TRIG-2). UNKNOWN and CONFLICTED are NOT falsy: a predicate evaluating to either does NOT fire (INV-TRIG-4) -- a trigger can never fire on a fact the system does not have.

referenced_subjects.description: Drives change-based re-evaluation. The evaluator re-runs this predicate when any referenced subject changes, which is what makes STATE triggers responsive rather than polled.

termination_proof.description: Output of the static termination checker. INV-TRIG-5: a predicate that cannot be proven terminating is rejected at registration (CI-024).

predicate_class.description: THE ANTI-CRON DISCRIMINATOR. A-029 part 3 requires at least one action in the endurance window to fire from a non-SCHEDULE class, and CI-026 rejects a registry containing only SCHEDULE triggers (INV-AUTO-5). A build whose entire trigger set is SCHEDULE-class is cron wearing autonomy's vocabulary.

priority.description: The priority lattice, stated as a rule rather than left to implementers: alarm_safety > active_user_task > ambience > proactive (REM-012 s3). alarm_safety is exempt from the interruption budget, ambience policy, resource yielding and quiet hours (INV-ALARM-3).

required_authority.description: Ceiling on the effective level actions under this trigger may reach. L5 is absent by construction: L5 is the level at which the subject must be a human (INV-SELF-3), so no trigger may reach it.

actuation_scope.description: REM-005. The two scopes are independently revocable by the safety interlock, so STOP_AUTONOMY preserves alarms (SR-043) while halting everything else.

cost_policy_ref.description: Resolved against contracts/policy/cost_policy.toml. Null means the default: free class only (INV-COST-6).

stop_conditions.description: RB-035 requires every autonomous unit of work to have one. An empty list is malformed.

report_noop.description: INV-TRIG-6: silence is a decision with provenance.

proactive_economics.description: Inputs to DF-PROACTIVE. 'decays' is load-bearing: information still useful in two hours does not justify interrupting now. High-value non-decaying items are QUEUED, never dropped.

provenance.description: INV-TRIG-7: a model may PROPOSE a trigger; it may not BE one. 'promoted_from_proposal' requires the REM-012 promotion gate AND a human merge, because autonomy/triggers/ is GOVERNED_PATHS surface 7 (REM-004).

status.description: SM-TRIGGER. PROPOSED -> ACTIVE is a prohibited transition.

allOf.$comment: INV-ALARM-3 -- only alarm-scoped triggers may carry alarm_safety priority.
DF-PROACTIVE requires economics for proactive contact.
A SCHEDULE-class predicate must still declare referenced subjects; a pure clock read is expressed through the schedule domain, not by omitting the field.
